# C2. Other countries {#esc-countries}

## What shapes the pension design in the U.S. and the UK {#esc-hosts}

The figure takes the counterfactuals of the paper's figure {{< var p.fig_US_ESC_overview >}} to the UK, at the UK's
own cost parameter, and sets it below the U.S. on the same axis. Each counterfactual is read twice, with the design pinned at the host's observed
value and with it chosen. Acute ageing ties both designs more closely to earnings, by about as much.
France's voting patterns move both toward flat benefits, the UK's by about as much at the lowest IES and by less
at the higher ones, since its own voting profile is already flatter than the U.S. one. France's income distribution moves the two designs in opposite
directions at every IES: on the U.S. it compresses relative incomes, on the UK it spreads them. On the UK, choosing
the design leaves the tax rate, the savings rate and the workweek close to the readings with the design pinned.

::: {.oa-explorer}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {counterfactuals, control, ROWS_CHOSEN, RHO, CHOSEN_OUTCOMES} from "./assets/oa.js"
esc = FileAttachment("_generated/data/ESC_Counterfactuals.csv").csv({typed: true})
escMain = esc.filter(d => d.source === "main" && d.spec === "size")
OBSERVED = ({"U.S.": esc.find(d => d.host === "US" && d.outcome === "theta" && d.reading === "pinned").baseline,
             "UK": esc.find(d => d.host === "UK" && d.outcome === "theta" && d.reading === "pinned").baseline})
viewof c2Out = control("radio", CHOSEN_OUTCOMES, {key: "outcome", label: "Outcome", value: "theta"})
counterfactuals(escMain, {rows: ROWS_CHOSEN, series: RHO, outcome: c2Out, mode: "chosen", width, observed: OBSERVED,
  facets: [{label: "U.S.", filter: d => d.host === "US"}, {label: "UK", filter: d => d.host === "UK"}]})
```
